title: Jeremiah Chapter 34 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 34 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 34 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 34.

questions.question: Who spoke the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: The word which came unto Jeremiah was from the LORD, as stated in Jeremiah 34:1.

questions.question: What did the LORD say He would do to the city?
questions.correctAnswer: Burn it with fire
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 34:2, the LORD declared that He would give the city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall burn it with fire.

questions.question: Who was the king of Judah during this prophecy?
questions.correctAnswer: Zedekiah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:2 specifically mentions Zedekiah as the king of Judah to whom the Lord spoke.

questions.question: True or False: Zedekiah was told he would die by the sword.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:4 states that Zedekiah shall not die by the sword.

questions.question: What shall happen to Zedekiah according to the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: He will die in peace
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:5 indicates that Zedekiah shall die in peace, unlike others who may die violently.

questions.question: True or False: The king of Babylon's army fought against Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:1 confirms that the king of Babylon's army fought against Jerusalem.

questions.question: What covenant did Zedekiah make with the people of Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: To proclaim liberty
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:8 states that Zedekiah made a covenant to proclaim liberty unto the people.

questions.question: According to the covenant, what were the people required to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Let their servants go free
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:9 indicates that every man should let his manservant and maidservant go free.

questions.question: True or False: The people obeyed the covenant and let their servants go free.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:10 tells us that the princes and people obeyed and let their servants go free.

questions.question: What did the people do after initially letting their servants go free?
questions.correctAnswer: They returned them to servitude
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 34:11, it is stated that afterward, they turned and caused the servants to return to servitude.

questions.question: What did the LORD say He made with their fathers?
questions.correctAnswer: A covenant
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:13 mentions that the LORD made a covenant with their fathers when He brought them out of Egypt.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD was pleased with the people's actions regarding their servants.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:16 shows that the people polluted the name of the LORD by bringing their servants back into subjection, which displeased Him.

questions.question: What consequence did the LORD proclaim for the people?
questions.correctAnswer: Destruction
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:17 indicates that the LORD proclaimed liberty for them to the sword, pestilence, and famine, which signifies destruction.

questions.question: In what manner will Zedekiah and his princes be delivered?
options: Into the hand of their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Into the hand of their enemies
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:21 states that Zedekiah and his princes will be given into the hand of their enemies.

questions.question: What will happen to the cities of Judah, according to the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: They will be burned
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:22 states that the LORD will cause them to fight against the city and burn it with fire.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 34 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 34 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 34:9, what command was given regarding Hebrew manservants and maidservants?
options: They should be set free and not serve their Hebrew brethren
They should be sold to foreign nations
questions.correctAnswer: They should be set free and not serve their Hebrew brethren
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:9 clearly commands that every Hebrew manservant and maidservant should be let go free and that no one should serve themselves of their Hebrew brother as a servant.

questions.question: What was the initial reaction of the princes and people when they heard the command to free their Hebrew servants, according to Jeremiah 34:10?
options: They obeyed and let them go free
They made a new law to keep them servants
questions.correctAnswer: They obeyed and let them go free
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:10 states that when the princes and people heard the command, they obeyed and released their servants, showing initial compliance with God's instruction.

questions.question: What did the people do after initially freeing their servants, according to Jeremiah 34:11?
options: They left them in the land to live independently
They took them back into servitude
They sent them to other nations
questions.correctAnswer: They took them back into servitude
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:11 explains that after freeing the servants, the people reversed their actions and caused them to return to servitude, violating the covenant they made.

questions.question: What covenant did God remind the people of in Jeremiah 34:13?
options: The covenant made at Mount Sinai
The covenant made when bringing the fathers out of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: The covenant made when bringing the fathers out of Egypt
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:13 speaks of the covenant God made with the fathers during the exodus from Egypt, reminding them of His command to let Hebrew servants go free every seven years.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 34:14, what was the specific command regarding Hebrew servants after six years of service?
options: They should be enslaved for life
They should be set free in the seventh year
They should be sold to foreigners
They should be punished if they disobey
questions.correctAnswer: They should be set free in the seventh year
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:14 commands that after six years of service, Hebrew servants must be freed in the seventh year, reflecting God's law of liberty and rest.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 34:15 describe the people's action when they initially proclaimed liberty to their neighbors?
options: They did wrong in God's sight
They did right and made a covenant before God
questions.correctAnswer: They did right and made a covenant before God
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:15 acknowledges that at first the people did right in God's sight by proclaiming liberty and making a covenant before Him in His house.

questions.question: What did the people do that polluted God's name, as described in Jeremiah 34:16?
options: They refused to build the temple
They returned the freed servants to servitude
questions.correctAnswer: They returned the freed servants to servitude
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:16 states that the people polluted God's name by taking back the servants and handmaids they had set free and making them serve again.

questions.question: Based on Jeremiah 34:17, what consequence does God proclaim for those who do not proclaim liberty to their brothers?
options: They will prosper in the land
They will be given liberty themselves
They will face sword, pestilence, famine, and exile
They will be forgiven without punishment
questions.correctAnswer: They will face sword, pestilence, famine, and exile
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:17 warns that those who disobey by not proclaiming liberty will suffer sword, pestilence, famine, and be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 34:18-19, who are specifically held accountable for breaking the covenant?
options: The princes, eunuchs, priests, and all the people
questions.correctAnswer: The princes, eunuchs, priests, and all the people
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:18-19 identifies all leaders and people—princes, eunuchs, priests, and the populace—as responsible for breaking the covenant made before God.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 34:20 say will happen to those who broke the covenant?
options: They will be protected by angels
Their dead bodies will be food for birds and beasts
They will be given a second chance
questions.correctAnswer: Their dead bodies will be food for birds and beasts
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:20 declares that those who transgressed the covenant will be handed over to enemies and their dead bodies will be left for birds and beasts, symbolizing utter desolation.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 34:21 describe the fate of King Zedekiah and his princes?
options: They will rule in peace forever
They will be given a new kingdom
They will be delivered into the hands of their enemies
They will be exalted by the people
questions.correctAnswer: They will be delivered into the hands of their enemies
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:21 states that Zedekiah and his princes will be given into the hand of their enemies, those seeking their lives, including the Babylonian army.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 34:22 say will happen to Jerusalem and the cities of Judah?
options: They will be rebuilt and inhabited
They will be taken, burned, and made desolate
They will be expanded and fortified
They will prosper under Babylonian rule
questions.correctAnswer: They will be taken, burned, and made desolate
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:22 prophesies that the Babylonians will return and capture Jerusalem, burn it, and make the cities of Judah desolate without inhabitants.

questions.question: True or False: According to Jeremiah 34:14, the fathers of Israel obeyed God's command to free Hebrew servants every seven years.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:14 explicitly states that the fathers did not obey God's command nor inclined their ear to it, showing disobedience.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 34:15 praises the people for making a covenant in the house called by God's name and proclaiming liberty.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:15 acknowledges that the people did right in God's sight by proclaiming liberty and making a covenant before Him in His house.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 34:11 says that after freeing their servants, the people permanently kept them free.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:11 reveals that the people reversed their decision and took back the servants into subjection, violating the covenant.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 34 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 34.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 34:17, what consequence does the LORD declare for those who have not hearkened to Him in proclaiming liberty to their brothers?
options: A liberty to the sword, pestilence, and famine, and removal into all kingdoms of the earth
Immediate exile without any further punishment
Restoration of the land and peace
questions.correctAnswer: A liberty to the sword, pestilence, and famine, and removal into all kingdoms of the earth
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:17 states that because they did not proclaim liberty, the LORD proclaims liberty to the sword, pestilence, and famine, and will remove them into all kingdoms of the earth. This is a judgment for breaking the covenant.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 34:18, what symbolic act is mentioned that the men who transgressed the covenant failed to honor?
options: Cutting the calf in twain and passing between its parts
Offering burnt sacrifices at the temple
Building an altar to the LORD
Writing the covenant on tablets of stone
questions.correctAnswer: Cutting the calf in twain and passing between its parts
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:18 refers to the covenant ceremony where the parties cut a calf in two and passed between the parts, symbolizing the seriousness of the covenant they made but failed to keep.

questions.question: Who are explicitly named in Jeremiah 34:19 as participants in the covenant ceremony of passing between the parts of the calf?
options: Princes of Judah, princes of Jerusalem, eunuchs, priests, and all the people of the land
The king and his family alone
questions.correctAnswer: Princes of Judah, princes of Jerusalem, eunuchs, priests, and all the people of the land
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:19 lists the princes of Judah, princes of Jerusalem, eunuchs, priests, and all the people of the land as those who passed between the parts of the calf, indicating a broad participation in the covenant.

questions.question: What fate does the LORD declare for the transgressors of the covenant in Jeremiah 34:20?
options: They will be given into the hand of their enemies, and their dead bodies will be food for the birds and beasts
They will be forgiven if they repent immediately
They will be restored to their land and honored
They will be taken captive but spared their lives
questions.correctAnswer: They will be given into the hand of their enemies, and their dead bodies will be food for the birds and beasts
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:20 declares that the transgressors will be delivered into their enemies’ hands and their bodies left to be scavenged by birds and beasts, a severe judgment showing disgrace and destruction.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 34:21, who will the LORD specifically give into the hand of their enemies?
options: Zedekiah king of Judah and his princes
questions.correctAnswer: Zedekiah king of Judah and his princes
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:21 specifically states that the LORD will give Zedekiah king of Judah and his princes into the hand of their enemies, showing that leadership will face judgment and captivity.

questions.question: What will the LORD command to happen to Jerusalem and the cities of Judah as described in Jeremiah 34:22?
options: The armies will return, fight, take the city, and burn it with fire, making the cities a desolation without inhabitants
The city will be spared and rebuilt
The city will be protected by angelic hosts
The people will be granted peace and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: The armies will return, fight, take the city, and burn it with fire, making the cities a desolation without inhabitants
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:22 says the LORD will command the Babylonian armies to return and destroy Jerusalem and the cities of Judah by fire, leaving them desolate and uninhabited.

questions.question: What covenant law from the time of the Exodus is referenced in Jeremiah 34:13-14 regarding Hebrew servants?
options: Letting every Hebrew servant go free at the end of seven years of service
Observing the Sabbath every seventh day
questions.correctAnswer: Letting every Hebrew servant go free at the end of seven years of service
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:13-14 recalls the covenant from Egypt where every Hebrew servant was to be released after six years of service, on the seventh year. This law was not heeded by their ancestors or themselves.

questions.question: What did the people do after proclaiming liberty to their servants, according to Jeremiah 34:11?
options: They took back the servants and handmaids and brought them into subjection again
They permanently freed all the servants
They sent the servants to another land
They gave the servants land and property
questions.correctAnswer: They took back the servants and handmaids and brought them into subjection again
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:11 states that after initially setting their servants free, the people reversed their decision and brought them back into servitude, violating their covenant.

questions.question: Which king of Judah did Jeremiah deliver the LORD’s message to in Jeremiah 34:2-3?
questions.correctAnswer: Zedekiah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:2-3 identifies Zedekiah as the king to whom Jeremiah was commanded to speak the message that the city would be handed over to Babylon and that he would be captured.

questions.question: True or False: According to Jeremiah 34:4, the LORD said that Zedekiah would die by the sword.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:4 explicitly states that Zedekiah would not die by the sword but would die in peace, unlike other kings before him.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 34:15 shows that proclaiming liberty and making a covenant before the LORD was initially regarded as doing right in His sight.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:15 affirms that proclaiming liberty to neighbors and making a covenant before the LORD was initially right in His sight, before they violated the covenant.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage closely relates to the covenant of freeing Hebrew servants after six years as mentioned in Jeremiah 34:14?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 21:2-6
questions.explanation: Exodus 21:2-6 outlines the law concerning Hebrew servants being freed after six years, which Jeremiah 34:14 references as the original covenant made at the Exodus.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Jeremiah 34:18-19 when the participants pass between the parts of the calf during the covenant ceremony?
questions.correctAnswer: A symbolic oath-taking ritual
questions.explanation: The cutting of the calf in two and passing between the pieces was a symbolic oath-taking ritual common in ancient Near Eastern covenant ceremonies, emphasizing the solemnity and binding nature of the agreement.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Hebrew word translated as 'proclaim liberty' in Jeremiah 34:8-9, and how does it relate to the Jubilee year concept found in Leviticus?
options: It means 'to announce freedom' and relates to the Jubilee year where slaves were released and land restored
It means 'to punish enemies' and relates to military conquest
It means 'to build a temple' and relates to religious festivals
It means 'to fast and pray' and relates to personal repentance
questions.correctAnswer: It means 'to announce freedom' and relates to the Jubilee year where slaves were released and land restored
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term here conveys announcing freedom or release, paralleling the Jubilee year in Leviticus 25 when slaves were freed and land returned, highlighting social justice themes in Jeremiah 34.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 34:22 foreshadow the historical event recorded in 2 Kings 25 regarding Jerusalem?
options: It predicts the Babylonian siege, capture, and burning of Jerusalem, fulfilling 2 Kings 25
It promises Jerusalem’s eternal peace contrary to 2 Kings 25
It foretells Jerusalem’s alliance with Egypt as in 2 Kings 25
It describes the rebuilding of Jerusalem after exile as in 2 Kings 25
questions.correctAnswer: It predicts the Babylonian siege, capture, and burning of Jerusalem, fulfilling 2 Kings 25
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:22 declares that the city will be captured and burned, which is historically fulfilled in 2 Kings 25 when Babylon destroyed Jerusalem and took the people captive.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 34 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 34 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 34:2 reveal about God's sovereignty over nations?
options: God permits nations to act independently of His will
God gives cities into the hand of foreign kings according to His purpose
God ignores the actions of earthly kings
God always protects Jerusalem from enemies
questions.correctAnswer: God gives cities into the hand of foreign kings according to His purpose
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:2 states that the LORD declares He will give the city into the hand of the king of Babylon, showing God's sovereign control over nations and their actions.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 34:4-5, what attribute of God is demonstrated in His promise to Zedekiah?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy and peace despite judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 4-5 reveal God's mercy in promising Zedekiah that he will not die by the sword but die in peace, showing God's compassionate attribute even in judgment.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 34:8-9 relate to the doctrine of social justice in the Old Testament?
options: It commands the release of Hebrew servants as an act of justice
It ignores the treatment of servants
questions.correctAnswer: It commands the release of Hebrew servants as an act of justice
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:8-9 commands proclaiming liberty to Hebrew servants, emphasizing God's concern for justice and freedom within the covenant community.

questions.question: What theological principle is illustrated by the people's initial obedience and subsequent disobedience in Jeremiah 34:10-11?
options: The instability of human faithfulness to God's covenant
questions.correctAnswer: The instability of human faithfulness to God's covenant
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 show that although the people initially obeyed God's command to free their servants, they later reversed their actions, demonstrating human weakness and covenant unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 34:13-14 teach about God's covenant with Israel regarding servants?
options: God permits perpetual slavery without release
God commanded the release of Hebrew servants every seven years
God made no covenant about servants
questions.correctAnswer: God commanded the release of Hebrew servants every seven years
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:13-14 recalls God's covenant at the Exodus commanding that Hebrew servants be freed after six years of service, with liberty proclaimed in the seventh year, emphasizing God's justice.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 34:15-16, what does God accuse the people of doing that polluted His name?
options: Returning their freed servants to bondage
questions.correctAnswer: Returning their freed servants to bondage
questions.explanation: Verses 15-16 indicate that although the people made a covenant to free servants, they polluted God's name by bringing them back into subjection, showing covenant breach and dishonor to God.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 34:17 depict God's justice in response to covenant-breaking?
options: God will proclaim a liberty to sword, pestilence, and famine
God will immediately forgive without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: God will proclaim a liberty to sword, pestilence, and famine
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:17 shows that God's justice involves severe judgment—liberty to sword, pestilence, and famine—as punishment for breaking His covenant.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Jeremiah 34:18-20 provide about covenant responsibility and divine judgment?
options: Covenant breakers will be protected from enemies
Those who transgress the covenant face judgment by enemies and desolation
questions.correctAnswer: Those who transgress the covenant face judgment by enemies and desolation
questions.explanation: Verses 18-20 teach that princes, priests, and people who broke the covenant will be delivered into the hands of their enemies, illustrating the serious consequences of covenant unfaithfulness.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 34:21-22, how does God's judgment fulfill the prophetic narrative concerning Jerusalem?
options: God will deliver Zedekiah and cause the city to be taken and burned
God will ignore the city's fate
questions.correctAnswer: God will deliver Zedekiah and cause the city to be taken and burned
questions.explanation: Verses 21-22 affirm that God will hand Zedekiah over to enemies and bring Babylon's army back to capture and burn Jerusalem, fulfilling the prophetic warnings of judgment.

questions.question: What attribute of God is emphasized by His promise to Zedekiah in Jeremiah 34:4?
options: God's mercy preventing death by the sword
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy preventing death by the sword
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:4 reveals God's mercy by promising Zedekiah that he will not die by the sword, highlighting God's compassionate care even amid judgment.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 34:1 introduce the historical context that shapes the theological message of the chapter?
options: By describing a peaceful era in Judah
By mentioning Nebuchadnezzar's siege of Jerusalem and his dominion
By focusing on internal politics only
questions.correctAnswer: By mentioning Nebuchadnezzar's siege of Jerusalem and his dominion
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:1 sets the stage by describing Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his army fighting against Jerusalem, grounding the theological message in historical judgment.

questions.question: What doctrinal teaching about God's covenant faithfulness and human failure is illustrated by comparing Jeremiah 34:13-14 with 34:15-16?
options: God's covenant is conditional on human obedience
Human failure nullifies God's covenant promises
God's covenant requires no response from people
questions.correctAnswer: God's covenant is conditional on human obedience
questions.explanation: Verses 13-14 describe God's covenant command about releasing servants, while 15-16 show the people's disobedience and pollution of God's name, illustrating that covenant blessings depend on obedience.

questions.question: What broader redemptive narrative connection is made in Jeremiah 34:13 with reference to the Exodus event?
options: The Exodus is irrelevant to covenant laws
God's covenant at Exodus established principles of liberation and justice
The Exodus only concerns land possession
questions.correctAnswer: God's covenant at Exodus established principles of liberation and justice
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:13 recalls God's covenant when bringing Israel out of Egypt, linking liberation from bondage to the command to free Hebrew servants, connecting to the redemptive theme of deliverance.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s judgments in Jeremiah 34 are arbitrary and cruel. What does Jeremiah 34:17-22 actually teach about God's justice and covenant accountability?
options: God issues just punishment proportionate to covenant violations
God's judgments are random acts of violence
questions.correctAnswer: God issues just punishment proportionate to covenant violations
questions.explanation: Verses 17-22 show that God's judgments come in response to covenant-breaking, particularly the failure to proclaim liberty, demonstrating divine justice and covenant accountability (cf. Ezekiel 18:20).

questions.question: What synthesis of Jeremiah 34:8-9 and 34:17 teaches about the relationship between covenant obedience and communal justice?
options: Obedience to covenant commands about liberty ensures communal blessing; disobedience brings judgment
Covenant commands are optional and have no impact on community
God values individual freedom above covenant obligations
Communal justice is unrelated to covenant faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to covenant commands about liberty ensures communal blessing; disobedience brings judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:8-9 commands proclaiming liberty to servants, while 34:17 pronounces judgment for failing to do so, teaching that covenant obedience is essential for communal justice and blessing.
